methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: PingThings to expand use of AI platform across Dominion Energy Virginia's grid data - Data Center Dynamics
signals.signal_reading: PingThings' AI platform expanding across Dominion's grid concentrates deep technical capability in NoVA's data center ecosystem while potentially creating statewide infrastructure benefits—a classic hub-and-spoke pattern that may widen rather than close regional capability gaps.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: This op-ed explicitly identifies the core problem: Virginia fixates on data center infrastructure while small businesses lack AI adoption pathways, signaling shallow engagement beyond metro hubs and missing the distributed capability-building that would enable 'Build It Yourself' scenarios.

signals.title: Virginia Tech tests thermal cameras and AI to warn drivers of animals near roads - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's applied AI research on wildlife detection demonstrates deep, locally-developed technical capability emerging outside NoVA—exactly the kind of distributed expertise and problem-solving that could seed peer networks across rural regions.

signals.title: Mace AI funds AI safety research at University of Virginia’s School of Data Science (UVA) - TheStreet
signals.signal_reading: Mace AI funding for UVA's School of Data Science concentrates advanced AI safety research in an academic hub, creating deep capability but raising questions about knowledge transfer to Virginia's broader business ecosystem and underserved regions.

signals.title: Roanoke County Schools opens new career and technology center - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke County's new career and technology center represents critical infrastructure for distributed technical workforce development—if curriculum includes AI/automation skills, it could enable the peer-to-peer capability building that distinguishes 'Build It Yourself' from shallow platform adoption.
